## Verdict: REJECT (four verification-checklist FAILs; one Important finding leaves acceptance criterion 3 unmet on the engine-subagent path)

## Issue Compliance

Reviewed against issue #1603: Establish that the review engine root arrived whole on the file-read path before executing it - criteria from workpad; scope unchanged. Requirement-based checklist items are included in the verification results below.

Criteria came from the `/prflow:implement` workpad comment - this run's authoritative set, possibly narrowed from the issue.

No divergence between the workpad's criteria and the issue body's.

Per-criterion assessment: AC1 satisfied (completeness established at the canonical site, merely-readable insufficient). AC2 satisfied (named terminal, body unusable, no repair). AC3 NOT ESTABLISHED - the dispatched engine subagent, which performs the fix loop's engine resolution on the path Step 1 tries first, receives no predicate at all (finding Important-1). AC4 satisfied (one canonical statement; no unreconciled "readable body" mirror survives). AC5 satisfied. AC6 satisfied (both skill roots byte-identical to the merge base and untouched). AC7 satisfied (two `Writing-skills evidence:` markers, four stated slots each). AC8 satisfied. AC9 satisfied (`lib + python tests` SUCCESS at the reviewed head, all five shards, zero skips).

## Verification Checklist Results

25 passed, 4 failed, 0 inconclusive - 1 via lite probe, 28 via agent.
Normalized (wording-only): 0; ineligible-on-field-defect FAILs: 0.

- VC-10: FAIL - "end of file is established ONLY by the shorter-than-position report or literally nothing" [skills/review-and-fix/references/loop-control.md:178]. Orchestrator adjudication: REFUTED BY DIRECT MEASUREMENT. The verifier chose its confirming offset from `wc -l` (340), an external counting tool the predicate explicitly forbids substituting. The reader's own whole read delivers through line 341; a confirming read at offset 342 returns "the file exists but is shorter than the provided offset (342). The file has 341 lines." - exactly the report the sentence names, and the ordinary outcome on a whole body. Even under the verifier's mistaken operand the "a blank line is content -> append and re-confirm" clause reaches 342 and establishes completeness in two reads. VC-11's independent empirical run reproduced both readings and returned PASS.
- VC-14: FAIL - "the engine root carries no boundary markers" [skills/review/SKILL.md]. PROBE-CONSTRUCTION ARTIFACT: the generator's `string_absent` probe scans for `prflow:review-ref` anywhere in the file; the two hits sit inside the fenced example documenting the marker format for the phase references. The claim itself is true - the root's first line is `---` and its last line is ordinary prose. The lite path has no normalization channel.
- VC-21: FAIL - "the degraded arm carries no completeness requirement for the predicate read" [skills/implement/phases/phase-3-fix-loop.md:39]. CLAIM-WORDING ARTIFACT: the arm does carry a requirement. The residual the verifier established is filed as Suggestion-1.
- VC-28: FAIL - "the Step 1 halt does not strand the mandatory per-iteration emit or a workpad terminal gate" [skills/review-and-fix/references/loop-control.md:188]. SUBSTANTIVE: the halt does strand the `iter-<N>.json` emit. Filed as Suggestion-5.

Passed items (25 of 29): VC-1 through VC-9, VC-11, VC-12, VC-13, VC-15 through VC-20, VC-22 through VC-27, VC-29.

## Code Review Findings

### Important / Major

1. The engine-subagent entry - the path Step 1 tries FIRST on every iteration - is not covered by the completeness predicate, and Step 4's disposition list has no arm for it. `loop-control.md`'s Engine-dispatch paragraph has an Agent-tool subagent resolve the candidate list and Read the engine root in a fresh context that does not hold `loop-control.md`; nothing instructs the parent to transcribe the predicate into that prompt, nor the subagent to read it - the exact remedy this same diff applied at `phase-3-fix-loop.md`'s degraded arm for the structurally identical case, with the stated reason that the file "did not load on this arm, so its text is not in your context". `shadow-review.md` added the completeness qualifier to the `unavailable` inline arm only. Step 4's disposition list names only Step 1 entry and Step 2.6 shadow entry; a subagent taking the terminal can do neither, having no loop to halt. The well-formedness fallback does not backstop it: a subagent that never learns the predicate accepts a truncated body and returns a well-formed `fanned-out` payload whose verdict carries the merge gate. Direct evidence - this review IS that dispatched subagent: its prompt carried no completeness predicate and it read the engine root with a single Read, issuing no confirming read. (raised by 2/3 agents)
2. On the implement tier's predicate-read-failure entry the durable Blocked record misattributes the failure to the engine root. `phase-3-fix-loop.md` routes a failed read of `references/loop-control.md` to the Blocked path "naming `engine-root: incomplete`", and that path's substitution "names that `SKILL.md` path"; `{path}` is unbound on this entry, so the record asserts a condition never tested about a file that is probably intact - while the same diff-added sentence claims the substitution exists "so the record names the real cause". Fail direction is closed, but this is the only human-facing artifact the halt produces. (raised by 2/3 agents)

### Suggestion / Minor

1. The predicate read on the degraded arm applies only the merely-readable test this change exists to close. `loop-control.md` carries a boundary-marker pair as its literal first and last lines and is 56,844 bytes (under the 61,750 ceiling), so naming that pair as the arm's acceptance test closes the gap at zero cost; today a truncated read returns the head, "succeeds", and delivers no predicate. (raised by 2/3 agents)
2. The Resolution arm's parenthetical "a permission failure among them" over-reaches: a harness- or sandbox-level policy refusal is also naturally called a permission failure yet affirms nothing about path existence, and under the parenthetical would select a candidate that does not exist on a consumer checkout. The governing clause is correct and the outcome fails closed, so this is a diagnosis edge, not a correctness hole. (raised by 1/3 agents)
3. An unestablished-resolution advance has no durable sink. "Naming in this run's report" is chat prose - no `--reflection`, no `--record-review-coverage` axis, no instruction to the implement orchestrator to look for it - so a self-review whose repo-root candidate was skipped can return a clean verdict produced by a vendored engine copy, with the downgrade visible only in a transcript that does not survive the run. (raised by 1/3 agents)
4. A newly reachable Blocked entry contradicts a pre-existing extension-tick rationale: the three Review extension rows are ticked "on every Phase 3 exit ... because those three extensions loaded on all of them", yet the new Blocked entry is reached from the degraded engine-read arm, entered precisely because the `Skill` call was refused twice. Pre-existing, diff-untouched prose; the file's unticked-row arm already supplies the correct behavior. (raised by 1/3 agents)
5. The Step 1 halt strands the fix loop's mandatory per-iteration `iter-<N>.json` emit, which is fused to Step 3's fix-commit moment the halt never reaches. Fail direction is closed - the terminal-complete gate is scoped to a `Complete` write - but the iteration's effectiveness record is silently absent. (from checklist item VC-28)
6. Shipped-prose cost audit (required by this repository's review extension). Every added block under `skills/**` carries a real instruction plus one consequence, so nothing is deletable wholesale; three clauses restate a rule another clause in the same block already binds - the in-line "starts later steps over undelivered lines" gloss versus the unestablished list's fourth shape; the two adjacent sentences carrying the single "no boundary markers, so no truncation notice" justification; and `phase-3-fix-loop.md`'s "which would otherwise mislabel the durable record" versus the Blocked path's own rationale. (orchestrator)

- Threshold resolved: `critical`.
- Self-contradicting-diff carve-out: evaluated, did not fire. Every diff-added factual claim checked (blank-line ratio, exemption roster, absence of boundary markers on the engine root, the three enumerated call sites, the end-of-file reader semantics) verified true against HEAD.
- Behavior-inert prose cap: evaluated, not applied - both Important findings dispute what the mechanism covers, a functional-coverage gap 4.1.5's sharpening rule forbids capping by that path.
- Rule 1 (any checklist FAIL -> REJECT): FIRES on VC-10, VC-14, VC-21, VC-28.
- Rule 3 (finding at or above `critical`): does not fire - no Critical finding.

phase3_findings.description: The engine-subagent entry — the path Step 1 tries FIRST on every iteration — is not covered by the completeness predicate, and Step 4's disposition list has no arm for it. loop-control.md's Engine dispatch paragraph has an Agent-tool subagent resolve the candidate list and Read the engine root in a fresh context that does not hold loop-control.md; nothing instructs the parent to transcribe the predicate into the subagent prompt, nor the subagent to read it — the exact remedy the same diff applied at phase-3-fix-loop.md's degraded arm for the structurally identical case. shadow-review.md added the completeness qualifier to the `unavailable` INLINE arm only, leaving the subagent arm on a bare 'resolves the engine directory per Step 1'. Step 4's disposition list names only Step 1 entry and Step 2.6 shadow entry; a subagent taking the terminal can do neither (it has no loop to halt). The well-formedness fallback does not backstop this: a subagent that never learns the predicate accepts a truncated body, returns a well-formed fanned-out payload, and its verdict carries the merge gate. Direct evidence: THIS review is that dispatched subagent — its prompt carried no completeness predicate and it read skills/review/SKILL.md with a single Read, issuing no confirming read. AC-3 ('no path is left with a weaker acceptance predicate than another') is therefore not met on that path.

On the implement tier's predicate-read-failure entry the durable Blocked record misattributes the failure to the engine root. phase-3-fix-loop.md routes a failed read of `references/loop-control.md` to the Blocked path 'naming engine-root: incomplete', and the Blocked path's substitution 'names that SKILL.md path'. `{path}` is unbound on that entry, so the record asserts a condition never tested about a file that is probably intact, sending the operator to the wrong file — while the same diff-added sentence claims the substitution exists 'so the record names the real cause'. Fail direction is closed; the defect is in the only human-facing artifact the halt produces. Remedy: bind `{path}` per entry, or give the predicate-read entry its own label.

The predicate read on the degraded arm applies only the merely-readable test this change exists to close: 'If that predicate read does not succeed'. loop-control.md carries a boundary-marker pair (`# Reference: Loop Control …` first line, `<!-- END loop-control.md -->` last line) and is 56,844 bytes, under the 61,750-byte ceiling, so a truncated read would return the head, 'succeed', and deliver no predicate — the predicate sits ~60% into the file. Naming that pair as the arm's acceptance test closes it at zero cost.

The Resolution arm's parenthetical 'a permission failure among them' over-reaches. A harness- or sandbox-level policy refusal, returned before the filesystem is touched, is also naturally called 'a permission failure' yet affirms nothing about existence — and under the parenthetical it would SELECT a candidate that does not exist on a consumer checkout and hard-stop at engine-root: incomplete rather than reaching the vendored engine one candidate later. The governing clause ('affirms the path exists') is correct and the outcome fails closed, so this is a diagnosis/availability edge, not a correctness hole; narrowing the example to an error that distinguishes non-existence from denial removes the ambiguity.

An unestablished-resolution advance has no durable sink. loop-control.md routes it to 'naming in this run's report which candidate it advanced past and why', and the self-review clause states the consequence plainly: the scan advances to a vendored copy, so the branch's own engine is NOT what reviewed the PR. 'This run's report' is chat prose: there is no --reflection for it, no axis in --record-review-coverage, and no instruction to the implement orchestrator to look for it, so a clean verdict can be produced by a fallback engine copy with the downgrade visible only in a transcript that does not survive the run. Note this shares a defect_signature with F4 but is a different defect.

A newly reachable Blocked entry contradicts a pre-existing extension-tick rationale. phase-3-fix-loop.md ticks three Review extension rows 'on every Phase 3 exit — … and the Blocked path alike, because those three extensions loaded on all of them'; the diff adds a Blocked entry reached from the degraded engine-read arm, which is entered precisely BECAUSE the Skill call was refused twice, so those extensions demonstrably did not load. The rationale is pre-existing and diff-untouched, and the file's unticked-row arm already supplies the correct behavior, so this is a note rather than a documented falsehood.

The Step 1 halt strands the fix loop's mandatory per-iteration iter-<N>.json emit. That emit is explicitly fused to Step 3's fix-commit moment; the halt stops before any mutation and never reaches Step 3, so the effectiveness record for that iteration is never written. Fail direction is closed — workpad.py's terminal-complete gate is scoped to a `Complete` write, so a `Blocked` write is not refused for lacking a review-coverage record — but the iteration's effectiveness record is silently absent.
